solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Everyone has attire on I fashioned with white wool, for example

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped or made up, so the preceding letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: everyone means all
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes getting dressed and making something in white wool.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL then ITERATION gives ALLITERATION. 'White wool' looks like part of the outfit, but it is the definition by example: both words start with W.
explanation.definitionFit: Two neighbouring words beginning with the same sound are an instance of alliteration.

clue.text: Lake once also largely surrounded by piece of land

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
surrounded by says the shortened word sits inside the next one

blocks.note: an area is a piece of land
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A lake that once existed was hemmed in by land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' signals that the lake has largely dried up, which is the fate of this Central Asian lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aral Sea was a huge inland lake that has mostly vanished, so it is a lake of former times.

clue.text: Relaxation time on lake: one's consumed by drink

indicators.note: something consumed by a drink goes inside it

blocks.note: a libation is a drink, often poured as an offering
an era is a period of time
L is the map abbreviation for lake
one is I, and one's is I plus S

explanation.surface: Taking time off at a lake, someone drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so time comes before lake. A libation was originally a drink poured out as an offering to a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberalisation is the loosening of rules or restrictions, a relaxation of controls.

clue.text: Bigwig is audibly tense

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so we want a word that is pronounced like the next one

blocks.note: to tense is to tighten, which is said much the same way

explanation.surface: An important person is noticeably nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, to tighten.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of great power or importance, like a bigwig.

clue.text: Official chooses to ignore top reviews

indicators.note: ignoring the top of a word drops its first letter

blocks.note: a ref is a referee, a sports official
to select is to choose

explanation.surface: A referee decides to disregard the best match reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' suggests the best reports, but it is the first letter, which in a down clue sits at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflects means thinks back over or considers, which is what someone who reviews does.

clue.text: Plant found in that room occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A plant is sometimes spotted in a particular room.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro is a tropical plant grown for its starchy root.

clue.text: Inflexible manifesto ultimately popular within British government

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it
within means the word for popular sits inside the word for government

blocks.note: its last letter
B is the abbreviation for British
the state is the government
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A political manifesto is rigid in its popularity inside a British administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obstinate is stubborn and refuses to change, so they are inflexible.

clue.text: Sailor needing energy opts to eat processed, starchy food

indicators.note: food that is processed is broken down and remade, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor
E is the symbol for energy
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hungry sailor decides to eat processed carbohydrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processed' sounds like the food is factory-made, but it is the signal to shuffle 'opts to eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacket potatoes are potatoes baked in their skins, a filling starchy dish.

clue.text: Quiet spot to grab shelter

indicators.note: to grab means one word takes hold of another and holds it inside

blocks.note: to spy is to spot or catch sight of
the lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: A peaceful place to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Quiet' and 'spot' look like nouns making a quiet spot; 'spot' is a verb meaning to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepy village is a quiet, drowsy one where little happens.

clue.text: Scope of the section pre-lunch?

blocks.note: AM marks the morning, the hours before noon
a bit is a section or piece

explanation.surface: A query about what is covered in some session held before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The section is placed after the morning marker, which is why it is 'section pre-lunch' read backwards in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit is a formal synonym for range or extent, the area something covers.

clue.text: Bar meeting the needs of Europeans on vacation? Incredible!

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been emptied out, leaving only its first and last letters

blocks.note: something for a purpose meets its needs
only the outside letters of the word remain
a tall story is an incredible one

explanation.surface: An amazed reaction to a pub designed to suit European holidaymakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but it is a verb here meaning to prevent. TALL means hard to believe, as in a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall something is to prevent it by acting first, as barring it does.

clue.text: One running off after second runner

indicators.note: after tells us the first-named piece follows the second-named one in the answer

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a machine that runs off copies

explanation.surface: Someone sets off in pursuit of an athlete in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running off' suggests fleeing, but it means producing copies, which is what a printer does.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is a runner over short distances, so it is one kind of runner.

clue.text: Difficulty caused by stinging sensation right away

indicators.note: the letter for right is sent away, so it is removed from the word

blocks.note: a prickle is a sharp stinging feeling
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A problem arises from a sudden sting felt immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as 'immediately', but it splits: R for right, and away to remove it from PRICKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pickle is an idiom for being in a tricky situation or predicament.

clue.text: Place somewhere in Scotland full of clubs, note

indicators.note: a town full of something holds it inside its own letters

blocks.note: Alloa is a town in central Scotland, north of the Forth
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Scottish town packed with golf clubs, noted down as a location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun going with 'somewhere', but it is the verb. Alloa is a small town in Clackmannanshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to assign or set aside, much as placing something puts it in a position.

clue.text: Trade vehicle held in on tracks

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
pent, as in pent-up, means confined
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on tracks

explanation.surface: A commercial vehicle is stuck on the railway lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held in' sounds like a container signal, but it is just PENT, the past participle of pen, meaning shut in.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry, working with wood, is a skilled trade.

clue.text: A little skill involved in work

indicators.note: something involved in another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: to ply is to work at, as in ply a trade
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Only a small amount of expertise goes into a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun for a job, but it is the verb, as in working at a trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly means to some degree, and 'a little' expresses that same modest extent as an adverb.

clue.text: Murder in detective's district

blocks.note: DI is a detective inspector, so detective's is DIS
a police officer's patch is their district

explanation.surface: A killing happens in the area an investigating officer covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them quickly, a euphemism for murder.

clue.text: Engineers arrange repair

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
to sort is to arrange in order

explanation.surface: Engineers organise mending some broken equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair' suggests mending, but it is the older sense of going somewhere, as in 'repair to the bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: To resort to a place is to go there, the same sense as repairing to a place.

clue.text: To some extent, it's a perfect flipping meal

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the phrase is used, so the answer lies within it
flipping turns the run of letters over so it reads backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the words 'it's a perfect'

explanation.surface: A frustrated diner says the meal is partly flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, but it signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal.

clue.text: Edits one nasty comment in the margin

indicators.note: nasty suggests something turned ugly and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor scribbles a cutting remark beside the text.
explanation.definitionFit: A side note is a remark written beside the main text, typically in the margin.

clue.text: Crooked dealer pocketing millions for gemstone

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of line, so the letters are twisted into a new order
pocketing means taking something inside, so the letter for millions goes in

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: A dishonest trader takes millions in exchange for a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' describes a dishonest dealer, but it means the letters of dealer are bent out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a precious green gem.

clue.text: Reduction of power, say, is a must for hitting green targets

definitions.text: a must for hitting green targets

blocks.note: P is the shortened form of power
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Cutting power is presented as essential for an environmental campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green targets' suggests environmental goals; in golf the green holds the hole, the target for a gentle stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the golf club used to roll the ball into the hole on the green.

clue.text: High-tech, special card allows guards entry at the front

indicators.note: at the front points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: sp is an abbreviation for special
an ace is a playing card
the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A special pass lets the security staff enter first.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-age describes something futuristic and technologically advanced, much as high-tech does.

clue.text: Waste from fruit and produce picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: to produce is to cause, which in a British accent is said like this

explanation.surface: Fruit waste and harvested produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' and 'picked' suggest farm crops; produce is the verb, to bring about. In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Cores are the inedible central parts of apples and pears, thrown away after eating.

clue.text: Life story captures heart of miserable writer

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so the middle letter is taken
captures means holds inside, so the short word wraps the chosen letter

blocks.note: a bio is a short biography
its central letter

explanation.surface: A biography portrays the core of a gloomy author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a pen: Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A biro is a ballpoint pen, something you write with.

clue.text: Those who are running maybe abruptly keel over

blocks.note: to stop short is to stop abruptly
a ship that lists leans over on its keel

explanation.surface: Runners in a race might suddenly collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests athletes, but it means running for a job or office.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the final group of candidates, those still running for a post or prize.

clue.text: Port and of course German wine

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port
ja is German for yes, as in 'of course'

explanation.surface: A list of drinks: port and, naturally, German wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified drink, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish wine from the region of that name.

clue.text: Put forward fantastic hot dishes? Yep!

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wild, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone serves up some amazing hot food and is asked to confirm it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hypothesise is to propose an idea as a possible explanation, i.e. put it forward.
